concepts.name: Green GDP: Definition and Conceptual Framework
key_dimensions: Distinction between conventional GDP and Green GDP — what gets added vs. subtracted
Formula: Green GDP = GDP − Cost of Environmental Degradation − Depletion of Natural Resources
UPSC trap: Green GDP can be lower OR higher than GDP depending on environmental investment accounting
Why standard GDP is called a 'welfare illusion' — ignores negative externalities and resource depletion

concepts.name: System of Environmental-Economic Accounting (SEEA)
key_dimensions: SEEA as the UN's statistical framework to integrate environment into national accounts — adopted 2012
Three components: SEEA Central Framework, SEEA Ecosystem Accounting (SEEA EA), SEEA Extensions and Applications
Difference between SEEA and SNA (System of National Accounts) — SEEA as a satellite account, not a replacement
India's status in adopting SEEA — partial implementation, challenges with data availability

concepts.name: Natural Capital Accounting (NCA)
key_dimensions: Definition of natural capital: stocks of natural assets (soil, water, air, biodiversity) that yield ecosystem services
Difference between 'capital stock' approach and 'flow' approach in accounting for nature
UPSC trap: Natural Capital ≠ just mineral resources; it includes non-marketed ecosystem services like pollination
Wealth of Nations Report (World Bank) — distinguishes produced capital, human capital, and natural capital

concepts.name: Genuine Progress Indicator (GPI)
key_dimensions: GPI adds social benefits and subtracts social costs that GDP ignores — income inequality, crime, pollution, volunteer work
Key distinction: GPI vs. HDI vs. Green GDP — GPI is broadest welfare measure covering social + environmental dimensions
Historical trend: GPI has stagnated or declined in many developed nations even as GDP rose — the 'threshold hypothesis'
UPSC trap: GPI is NOT an official UN or government statistic; it is an academic/advocacy measure

concepts.name: Human Development Index (HDI) as a Welfare Measure
key_dimensions: Three dimensions: Health (life expectancy), Education (mean + expected years), Income (GNI per capita at PPP)
HDI does NOT include environmental sustainability — IHDI (Inequality-adjusted HDI) corrects for inequality but not ecology
UPSC trap: HDI uses GNI per capita, NOT GDP per capita — distinction between resident-based and production-based measures
Planetary Pressures-Adjusted HDI (PHDI) — new UNDP index that discounts HDI for carbon footprint and material footprint

concepts.name: Inclusive Wealth Index (IWI)
key_dimensions: Developed by UNEP/IPBES — measures total wealth including produced capital, human capital, and natural capital
Unlike GDP (flow measure), IWI is a stock/wealth measure — tracks long-run sustainability, not just annual output
UPSC trap: A country can have rising GDP but falling IWI — indicating unsustainable development (e.g., resource-exporting nations)
India's performance on IWI — natural capital per capita declining despite GDP growth

concepts.name: Adjusted Net Savings (ANS) / Genuine Savings
key_dimensions: World Bank metric: ANS = Gross National Savings − Fixed Capital Depreciation − Natural Resource Depletion − Pollution Damage + Education Expenditure
Negative ANS signals that a country is on an unsustainable development path — 'eating into its wealth'
UPSC trap: Education expenditure is ADDED in ANS (treated as investment in human capital), unlike in GDP where it's consumption
ANS vs. Green GDP — ANS is a savings/investment sustainability indicator; Green GDP is an output/income indicator

concepts.name: Wealth Accounting and Valuation of Ecosystem Services (WAVES) Partnership
key_dimensions: World Bank-led global partnership to operationalize natural capital accounting in national statistics
India as a pilot country under WAVES — focus on forests, water, and land accounts
Distinction between WAVES (implementation platform) and SEEA (methodological framework) — WAVES uses SEEA methodology
Challenge of valuing non-marketed ecosystem services — contingent valuation, hedonic pricing, travel cost methods

concepts.name: Ecosystem Services Valuation Methods
key_dimensions: Four categories: Provisioning (food, water), Regulating (climate regulation, flood control), Cultural (recreation), Supporting (nutrient cycling)
Valuation approaches: Market price method, Replacement cost method, Contingent Valuation Method (CVM), Benefit Transfer
UPSC trap: Supporting services are NOT directly valued in SEEA EA to avoid double-counting — only final ecosystem services are valued
The Economics of Ecosystems and Biodiversity (TEEB) initiative — mainstreaming biodiversity values into economic decisions

concepts.name: Resource Rent and Depletion in National Accounts
key_dimensions: Resource rent = Revenue from resource extraction − All costs of extraction (including normal return on capital)
Depletion cost = Resource rent × (Quantity extracted / Proven reserves) — the 'El Serafy method'
UPSC trap: In standard GDP, extraction of oil/minerals is counted as income; in Green GDP, it is reclassification of wealth, not income
Hotelling's Rule — optimal depletion path where resource rent rises at the rate of interest — theoretical basis for depletion accounting

concepts.name: Gross Environment Product (GEP)
key_dimensions: China's pioneering concept — monetary value of ecosystem services provided by natural ecosystems in a given area and period
GEP complements GDP — policy goal of ensuring GEP does not decline even as GDP grows
UPSC trap: GEP measures ecosystem service flows, NOT the stock of natural capital — contrast with IWI
India's potential for GEP accounting — relevance for state-level forest and wetland accounting

concepts.name: Happiness and Well-being Indices: GNH and World Happiness Report
key_dimensions: Gross National Happiness (GNH) — Bhutan's framework; 4 pillars: sustainable development, cultural preservation, environmental conservation, good governance
GNH vs. GDP: GNH is a governance philosophy, not a statistical measure — UPSC trap on this distinction
World Happiness Report (WHR) — uses Cantril Ladder (life evaluation score) + 6 variables: GDP/capita, social support, healthy life expectancy, freedom, generosity, corruption perceptions
UPSC trap: WHR is NOT a UN official report — it is published by the Sustainable Development Solutions Network (SDSN)

concepts.name: Stiglitz-Sen-Fitoussi Commission and 'Beyond GDP' Framework
key_dimensions: Commissioned by French President Sarkozy (2008) — report argued GDP is inadequate for measuring societal well-being
Key recommendations: measure household income/consumption, include non-market work, add sustainability dashboard
Multi-dimensional dashboard approach vs. single composite index — UPSC angle on tradeoffs of aggregation
Influence on EU's 'Beyond GDP' initiative and OECD Better Life Index

concepts.name: OECD Better Life Index (BLI)
key_dimensions: 11 dimensions: Housing, Income, Jobs, Community, Education, Environment, Civic Engagement, Health, Life Satisfaction, Safety, Work-Life Balance
Interactive/customizable index — users assign their own weights to dimensions; UPSC trap: no single official ranking exists
Comparison with HDI: BLI is richer in social dimensions but limited to OECD countries; HDI has global coverage
Environment dimension in BLI measures air quality and water quality — not full natural capital accounting

concepts.name: Carbon Accounting and GDP: Green National Accounts
key_dimensions: Carbon cost internalization: Social Cost of Carbon (SCC) — damage caused by emitting one additional tonne of CO2
If SCC is incorporated into national accounts, GDP of fossil-fuel-dependent economies falls significantly
UPSC trap: Carbon credits and carbon markets generate GDP in standard accounts but represent offsetting of negative externalities
India's NDC targets and the implication for coal/fossil fuel asset stranding on national wealth accounts

concepts.name: India-Specific Initiatives: National Resource Accounting and Green Accounting for Indian States
key_dimensions: Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI) — pilot natural resource accounting for forests, land, water
'Green Accounting for Indian States Project (GASP)' — academic initiative by GIPE/CPR estimating state-level environmental income
UPSC trap: India does NOT yet publish an official Green GDP figure — all estimates are academic/pilot exercises
Forest Survey of India (FSI) reports ecosystem service values — but not yet integrated into official national accounts

concepts.name: Limitations and Criticisms of Green GDP
key_dimensions: Valuation problem: Many ecosystem services have no market price — subjective and contested monetary values
Political economy challenge: Countries with resource-dependent growth resist Green GDP as it shows lower 'real' growth
China abandoned its Green GDP pilot in 2007 due to political resistance from provinces showing negative Green GDP
UPSC trap: Green GDP is NOT the same as Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) measurement — SDGs use a multi-indicator framework, not a single aggregate

concepts.name: Satellite Accounts in National Accounting
key_dimensions: Satellite accounts extend SNA without disrupting core GDP — examples: environmental satellite accounts, health satellite accounts, tourism satellite accounts
UPSC trap: Satellite accounts are supplementary, NOT replacements for GDP — they sit 'alongside' the core SNA
India's Tourism Satellite Account (TSA) and proposed Environmental Satellite Account under SEEA
Household Production Satellite Account — values unpaid domestic and care work (predominantly women's labor) excluded from GDP

concepts.name: Multi-Dimensional Poverty Index (MPI) as a Welfare Alternative
key_dimensions: UNDP/OPHI index — 3 dimensions (Health, Education, Living Standards) across 10 indicators; uses Alkire-Foster methodology
UPSC trap: MPI ≠ Below Poverty Line (BPL) in India — BPL uses income/consumption threshold; MPI is multi-dimensional deprivation
India's NITI Aayog publishes National MPI — 2023 report showed significant reduction in multidimensional poverty
MPI does NOT include environmental sustainability — contrast with Green GDP and IWI which do

concepts.name: Welfare Cost of Pollution and the 'Genuine GDP' Concept
key_dimensions: Air and water pollution impose welfare costs (health expenditure, productivity loss) that reduce true welfare even as GDP rises
Paradox of pollution and GDP: GDP can RISE due to pollution — spending on healthcare and cleanup is counted as output ('defensive expenditures')
UPSC trap: In standard GDP, defensive expenditures (treating pollution-related illness) add to GDP — a fundamental flaw in welfare measurement
WHO/World Bank estimates: Pollution costs India approximately 8.5% of GDP annually — factoring this in would significantly reduce 'Genuine GDP'
